clue.text: Body of man hidden in vehicle

indicators.note: the man's name is concealed inside the vehicle, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man's corpse is found concealed in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, a dead human body.

clue.text: Young creature shelled coming out of pen

definitions.text: Young creature shelled coming out of pen

parts.words: Young creature shelled coming out of pen
parts.note: a pen is a female swan; her baby hatches from its egg, leaving the shell, while the surface suggests something escaping an enclosure

explanation.surface: A young animal, bombarded with shells, breaks out of its enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' reads as an enclosure or a writing tool; in birdwatching it is a female swan, whose hatchling emerges from the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is the young of a swan, and a pen is the female swan that lays the egg.

clue.text: Southern girl in set-up supplying cards

indicators.note: the southern girl is placed inside the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: set, as in laid the table, means laid
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A southern girl in some arrangement hands out playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' looks like one noun, but 'set' gives LAID and 'up' turns it to DIAL, which holds S and MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: To get your cards is a British idiom for being sacked, so cards means dismissal from a job.

clue.text: Alternative verse added to songbooks

indicators.note: the verse letter is attached in front of the rest

parts.note: split into song and books: a song is an aria
the books here are NT, the New Testament

explanation.surface: A different verse is included in the hymn books.
explanation.walkthrough: One printed word does two jobs as two pieces once split at its middle; the books are the New Testament, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant is another form or version, an alternative to the usual one.

clue.text: Like crocodiles ruining a Nile trip

indicators.note: the words a Nile trip are spoiled and rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Crocodiles spoil a holiday cruise on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodiles are reptiles, so something like them is reptile-like.

clue.text: Refuse game originally burnt by mistake

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word burnt

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Something in a game was set alight by accident and thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun, waste, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is waste matter thrown away, which is what refuse means as a noun.

clue.text: Grooms' mates head off for outings on horseback

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for grooms' partners is removed

parts.note: brides are the women grooms marry

explanation.surface: The brides of the grooms go off on horseback outings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grooms' suggests stable hands, fitting the horses, but here they are bridegrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides are trips taken on a horse.

clue.text: Obstacle Scottish author found on river

indicators.note: in a down clue the author sits on top of the river letter

parts.note: J. M. Barrie, Scottish author of Peter Pan

explanation.surface: An obstacle was discovered on a river by a Scottish writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is something that blocks the way, an obstruction.

clue.text: Badly framed, extremely dingy pastoral scene

indicators.note: framed means the first piece surrounds the second like a picture frame

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outer letters of dingy

explanation.surface: A rustic picture, poorly framed and very drab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly framed' reads as a criticism of the picture; in fact ILL frames DY, the first and last letters of 'dingy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a charming rural scene or a poem describing one.

clue.text: It's old hat to put in country dances for festivals

indicators.note: the old-hat letters are placed inside the dances

parts.note: a hay is a country dance with interweaving figures
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Folk dancing at festivals is old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like one phrase meaning stale; it splits into O and LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidays were originally holy days, religious festivals.

clue.text: Good trap's designed for slug, say

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new design

parts.note: the possessive here keeps its S as a letter: trap's spelt out

explanation.surface: A good trap is built to catch slugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is an example of a gastropod, the mollusc class including snails and slugs.

clue.text: Sail in one of the Queens, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigged ship
a member of the monarch's family, such as a queen

explanation.surface: Raising a sail aboard a ship called Queen something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Cunard liners named Queen; separately, a sail and a member of royalty share this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small high sail and a member of the monarch's family.

clue.text: Punishment for murdering a girl found on moor

parts.note: an eric was the fine paid for killing someone under old Irish law

explanation.surface: A girl's body is found on the moor and someone must pay for the killing.
explanation.walkthrough: An eric is an obscure old Irish blood-fine. The definition is playful: Erica is a girl's name and the botanical name for heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heath plants growing on moors, and like Heather it is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Dines out, accepting work introduced gradually

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the other piece
out signals that the letters of dines go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Someone eats out after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the eating word into INSED, and 'accepting' means that shuffle takes in the farming verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to introduce it into the mind slowly over time.

clue.text: Two things models generally are, advantageously placed

parts.note: artists' models are typically seated, posing
fashion models are typically good-looking

explanation.surface: A remark about models being well positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in a fortunate, comfortable position.

clue.text: A couple of chaps making headgear

parts.note: Glen is a man's name
Garry is a man's name

explanation.surface: Two men make a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The two names are both men's names; together they give a Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A glengarry is a Scottish brimless cap with a crease down the crown and ribbons at the back.

clue.text: It makes its mark twice daily at the seaside

definitions.text: It makes its mark twice daily at the seaside

parts.words: It makes its mark twice daily at the seaside
parts.note: the sea rises and falls twice each day, leaving a line on the beach

explanation.surface: Something leaves its trace on the coast twice every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Water brought in by the tides reaches the high-water mark on the shore each high tide.

clue.text: Tailless dog suitably accommodated in home

indicators.note: the word for suitably is housed inside the shortened dog
the last letter of the dog is cut off

parts.note: a dingo is an Australian wild dog
well means suitably, fittingly

explanation.surface: A dog with no tail is comfortably housed at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' turns DINGO into DING, which holds WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house, a place where someone lives.

clue.text: Having influential friends like Elsie and her sisters?

definitions.meaning: knowing people of power and status
in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters, Elsie, Lacie and Tillie, who lived at the bottom of a treacle well

explanation.surface: Elsie and her sisters know important people.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading needs the Dormouse's tale at the Mad Tea-Party: the three sisters lived in a well, so are linked to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-connected means having family or social ties to powerful people.

clue.text: Italian city's novel romance

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: An Italian city's new love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun about a romance; it is an adjective, new.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a city in Lombardy, famed for violin makers.

clue.text: Remarkable person appearing in drag for musical series

indicators.note: the remarkable person shows up inside the word for drag

parts.note: to tow is to drag
a oner is British slang for an exceptional person

explanation.surface: An outstanding performer appears in drag in a musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' suggests cross-dressing; it means TOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone row is an ordering of the twelve chromatic notes used in serial music.

clue.text: Hammer and spades on shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue spades sits on top of the shelf

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: Tools such as a hammer and spades kept on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' reads as one item in a list of tools; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge, or sledgehammer, is a large heavy hammer.

clue.text: Untidy American changing beginning of dance

indicators.note: the first letter of the dance is swapped for another

parts.note: the jitterbug is a lively swing dance

explanation.surface: A messy American alters the start of a dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the J of JITTERBUG for L; the clue leaves the new letter to the crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is American slang for someone who drops rubbish in public.

clue.text: Old Asian taking so long to get over river

indicators.note: in a down clue the farewell goes over, above, the river letter

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye

explanation.surface: An old Asian takes a long time to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' reads as duration; it is a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars were a Turkic people of Central Asia.

clue.text: Primate, for example -one beginning to pontificate when retired

indicators.note: when here means while in, so one and P lie inside the bed

parts.note: to retire is to go to bed
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the first letter of pontificate is taken

explanation.surface: A primate, perhaps a bishop, starts to pontificate after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, fitting 'pontificate', but means an ape: any two-footed animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Primates such as humans walk on two feet, making them two-footed animals.

clue.text: Rail supporter wanting modern English line

parts.note: new means modern

explanation.surface: A banister post lacking a modern English line.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the post at the foot of a staircase holding up the handrail.

clue.text: Start to work in plain trousers

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters of plain trousers

explanation.surface: Someone begins work wearing plain trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is a musical or literary work, whose opening it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Summed up, holy-sounding female having left

indicators.note: the female letter departs from the longer word

parts.note: holy sounds like holey, full of holes, which is perforated

explanation.surface: A pious-sounding woman left after summing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holy-sounding' gives holey, PERFORATED; F leaving makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To perorate is to deliver the concluding summary of a speech.

clue.text: Film star's anthology

definitions.meaning: Judy ..., star of The Wizard of Oz
a collection of short literary pieces or poems

explanation.surface: A film star's collection of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Judy Garland was a Hollywood star, and a garland is an old word for a literary anthology.

clue.text: Irishman's call to wise men, say, to identify churchyard plant

indicators.note: spoken in a stage Irish accent, where th is said as t

parts.note: the wise men, the Magi, were three, so one would hail them as you three

explanation.surface: An Irishman addresses some wise men to point out a churchyard tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a stereotyped Irish accent 'three' is said 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are traditionally planted in English churchyards.
